newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car sales won't tumble after tax hike--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan car sales won't tumble after tax hike--EPA.

text.p: Car sales in Japan will not drop sharply after the consumption tax is raised on April 1, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso said on Tuesday.
Aso said he did not rule out the possibility that the recent strength in domestic car sales was supported by a rush of buying ahead of the planned tax rise.
But he added that sales efforts by individual car manufacturers and replacement demand for new cars were the main factors behind the robust sales.
"So I don't feel that (car sales) will all of a sudden plummet from April," Aso said.
He also said the economy was likely to achieve the government's target of 1.9 percent growth for the next fiscal year starting on April 1.
Aso said there were differing views on the outlook for private consumption, but added that steady capital spending and rising production would enable the economy to reach the 1.9 percent goal.
